video_title: Does Trae Young’s deal with the Wizards lock in AJ Dybantsa at No. 1? | NBA Today

quotes.speaker: Jeremy Woo
quotes.summary_phrase: Jeremy Woo on the Wizards' draft decision between Dybantsa and Peterson
quotes.excerpt: the margin between them is very thin. Now knowing that this large financial commitment is coming to Trae
quotes.quote: The Wizards have been quiet about this. They have been taking their time deciding between AJ Dybantsa and Darryn Peterson. Two guys who the margin between them is very thin. Now knowing that this large financial commitment is coming to Trae Young, who they traded for to build around, you wonder about fit. You wonder about Darryn Peterson who wants to play point guard at the next level. Does it make sense for him in Washington or do you go with Dybantsa who gives them a different type of athlete, a guy who can get downhill? It changes the dynamic of their team building forward because you know four years is locked in, that's the duration of a rookie deal, so it lines up with whatever max extension you are going to give the next guy.

quotes.speaker: King McClure
quotes.summary_phrase: King McClure argues AJ Dybantsa is the best prospect in the draft
quotes.excerpt: when you ask the question of how can you make an impact greater than just scoring, it's AJ
quotes.quote: I am going with AJ Dybantsa. When I look at the full grand scape of things, I always ask myself, how can you make an impact outside of scoring? We know that AJ led the country in scoring. But Darryn Peterson had his moments, really loud moments, where he put on a show and showed us his shot-making was elite. So I think that when we ask the question of how can you make an impact greater than just scoring, it's AJ because he had 11 games where he had five assists or more. To me, when you talk about his playmaking at his size, that's what separates him. When we sat down with Kevin Young at the combine, he said his passing ability is his most underrated thing in his game that nobody talks about.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst reports the Wizards are still considering Darryn Peterson
quotes.excerpt: This doesn't preclude them, they say, from taking Peterson with the number one pick.
quotes.quote: Speaking to the Wizards today, they are very happy to get Trae Young under contract. This doesn't preclude them, they say, from taking Peterson with the number one pick. Now, whether we believe that or not is a different story, but they are saying that they will take, and you know, they have done a very good job to this point of keeping their cards close to their vest. They try to keep doing that. However, I think the league will probably say this is an indication that they will follow what Jeremy has projected, which is AJ Dybantsa first.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on the Utah Jazz's interest in Cameron Boozer
quotes.excerpt: there are executives and scouts that I've talked to who have said to me, the Utah Jazz should seriously consider Boozer
quotes.quote: There are executives and scouts that I've talked to who have said to me, the Utah Jazz should seriously consider Boozer at number two. However, I say to them, so you are telling me if Dybantsa or Peterson is there, that you would pass on them? And the answer is mostly like, yeah. So I think in other years, Boozer would go number one and we would have celebrated it days and weeks in advance. But that's not the case.

quotes.speaker: AJ Dybantsa
quotes.summary_phrase: AJ Dybantsa on his expectations for his rookie season
quotes.excerpt: making it to the playoffs. I think all the teams in the top five are going to make it to the playoffs
quotes.quote: Making it to the playoffs. I think all the teams in the top five are going to make it to the playoffs, so wherever team I go to make it to the playoffs and be an immediate impact. But rookie of the year is also on the goal list.

quotes.speaker: Caleb Wilson
quotes.summary_phrase: Caleb Wilson on proving his doubters wrong by reaching the NBA
quotes.excerpt: it proves all the people that, you know, didn't believe in me wrong
quotes.quote: It proves all the people that, you know, didn't believe in me wrong, but I really, like I said, I just focus on myself. I feel like it's really important to have that opportunity to play in the NBA, but you know, proving myself right is going to keep going. I want to be the rookie of the year and also want to have a great career.

quotes.speaker: Caleb Wilson
quotes.summary_phrase: Caleb Wilson on comparisons to Kevin Garnett
quotes.excerpt: I also don't like to be compared to Hall of Famers, I feel like that's like respectful to them.
quotes.quote: I think we're kind of different. I also don't like to be compared to Hall of Famers, I feel like that's like respectful to them. Like if I was a Hall of Famer and I did and I won championships, like I don't know if I would be okay with someone calling a guy who hasn't proven anything, me, or similar to me. But I feel like we definitely have similarities. I feel like I do things way different than him in some aspects though, like I'm more of a dribbler, I can create for myself a little bit more, and KG was just a dog. I feel like we have a similar mentality and approach towards the game.
